newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chocolate sales lull dampens cocoa demand.
newsitem.headline: German chocolate sales lull dampens cocoa demand.

text.p: Physical cocoa markets in Germany were marking time because industry was preoccupied with unsatisfactory chocolate sales, traders said on Wednesday.
"Raw materials buyers say they need less cover because some plants are scheduled to undergo maintenance shutdowns during a number of public holidays in May," one trader said.
"It's a polite way of saying their sales are down."
Sellers also rolled forward cocoa butter positions, with demand equally depressed although butter ratios held steady.
Traders said futures markets and sterling levels were too high to offer buying opportunities.
The British currency jumped over two pfennigs earlier today while futures were mixed with July last two stg down at 998 stg/tonne.
News of good West African crops and shrinking global deficit forecasts for the 1996/97 season had been factored into the market, which needed new input from fundamentals, traders said.
West African beans were quoted little changed on the week at 2.71 marks/kg cif for May/June, 2.75 in the third and 2.72 in the fourth quarter.
Traders said buyers were looking for 2.65 marks spot and most recent trades at the end of April had been done at 2.62.
The cocoa butter ratio was at 2.40 spot, at 2.45 for the third and at 2.52 for the fourth quarter.
Implied mark prices liquid ex-works were marginally down on the week at 6.70 marks for May/June, 6.84 marks for the third quarter and 6.94 marks for the fourth.
